findings.claim: getRelayer now selects NoFeeCampaignRelayer whenever the config service reports NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN, removing the prior check that also required a local relay.noFeeCampaign[chainId] entry. The relay() method then reads this.relayConfiguration[chainId].maxGasLimit without a guard, while its sibling methods canRelay and getRelaysRemaining do have such a guard, so a chain flagged NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN in the config service but not present locally (locally only chains 1 and 11155111 are defined) will cause POST /v1/chains/:id/relay to throw a TypeError and return a 500.

This is the call site that reaches the unguarded no-fee-campaign relayer logic, and nothing upstream (LimitAddressesMapper, controller filters) prevents the resulting TypeError from propagating as an unhandled 500.

A null relayer type now throws NoRelayerDefinedError and returns 403, whereas previously any unconfigured chain fell back to DailyLimitRelayer with an explicit backward-compatibility comment; this fallback has been removed.

The schema's .catch(null) turns both a missing relayerType field and any unrecognized value into null, which now results in a 403 instead of the previous daily-limit fallback, affecting both POST relay and GET relays-remaining endpoints.

.env.sample.json defaulted RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS to Sepolia only, meaning most chains that currently relay successfully do so via the fallback that was removed; if this deploys before the config service sets relayerType on every chain, relaying on those chains will start returning 403 immediately.

The new 403 path is not tested end to end: no integration test covers a null or GTF relayer type on POST relay or GET relays-remaining, so the filter wiring and response body for this case are unverified.

No controller test covers RELAY_FEE routing, and if RelayerNotAvailableExceptionFilter were dropped from either @UseFilters decorator, the existing test suite would still pass, meaning the wiring isn't actually protected by tests.

The .catch(null) silently converts an unknown relayer type value from the config service (e.g. a new, unhandled value) into a 'no relayer defined' result with no logging, making a misconfiguration indistinguishable from an intentional block. The swallowed value should be logged.

The shared chains domain schema now imports from modules/relay, while relay and fees already import ChainsModule, creating a bidirectional dependency between the modules (no runtime cycle currently since the entity itself has no imports). The RelayerType enum would better belong with the chain entity or in a shared domain location.

The file still documents the removed RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS variable (marked required: true) and RELAY_FEE_CHAIN_IDS, which are no longer used; yarn env:validate will warn about both as extra variables.
The relay endpoints lack an @ApiForbiddenResponse decorator even though 403 is now a documented possible outcome; RelayDenied has the same gap, predating this change.

RelayerType is imported twice in this file, once as a value and once as a type alias (RelayerTypeValue), whereas relay-manager.interface.ts imports it only once; a single import would suffice since the name serves as both value and type.
